stem: Yash must construct rectangle $ABCD$ so that diagonal $AC$ divides $\angle DAB$ into $60^{\circ}$ and $30^{\circ}$. The diagram shows the right angle at $A$ and those parts along diagonal $AC$.

options.text: Call the finished figure diagonal $AC$ only.
Say that drawing diagonal $AC$ is what creates rectangle $ABCD$.
Use $\angle DAB=90^{\circ}$, so the $60^{\circ}$ part leaves $30^{\circ}$; then place sides and vertex $D$ from that split.
Choose the plan only because $60$ is the largest printed angle number among $60$, $30$, and $90$.

teacher.key_rationale: A rectangle corner is 90°, so a 60° part of the diagonal split leaves 30°, locating the next sides and D. Naming only the diagonal substitutes a label. Saying the diagonal creates the rectangle reverses construction. Picking the largest print is surface capture.
teacher.figure_note: figure add: rectangle with 60°/30° diagonal split at A
